rationale: The proposed Stonepeak investment in New England Power transmission assets is a false identity and perimeter conflation. New England Power Company remained National Grid USA's wholly owned regulated transmission subsidiary. Stonepeak's similarly named holding was Canal Power Holdings, a separate 1.6 GW merchant-generation portfolio acquired in 2018-2019 and sold entirely to JERA, closing December 1, 2022.
recommendedChanges: Exclude the proposed New England Power transmission assets holding and do not create a company or Stonepeak ownership period.
Preserve New England Power Company as a National Grid-controlled regulated transmission utility, not a Stonepeak PortCo.
Treat Stonepeak New England Power and Canal Power Holdings as a separate realized merchant-generation platform if that historical holding is reconciled elsewhere.
Do not convert the descriptive census label into a legal company name and do not count individual transmission lines, substations or New England Hydro-Transmission affiliates as Stonepeak holdings.
unresolvedQuestions: The exact JERA acquisition affiliate name was not publicly disclosed in the reviewed party announcement.
Canal III, Bucksport and exit prices and the Bucksport investment vehicle were not publicly disclosed.
NEP preferred-share holders and voting rights were not needed to resolve National Grid control and no Stonepeak evidence was found.
